standard: NFPA 13 (2019 edition) - Figure 19.3.3.1.1 density/area curves (p. 13-162), Table 19.3.3.1.2 hose stream + duration (p. 13-162), Table 10.2.4.2.1(a)/(b)/(c) protection areas (p. 13-78 onward)
note: density/designArea are the MINIMUM points of each density/area curve (lowest density at its paired maximum area), which is the usual starting design point - not the only valid point on the curve. A designer may select any point along the curve, so these are presets, not limits. hoseStreamGpm/durationMinutes duplicate the coarser LIGHT/ORDINARY/EXTRA rows in reference/storage/fire-water-duration.json (which does not split the Ordinary/Extra groups); see README.md. Where NFPA 13 gives a duration range, the conservative upper bound is used.
verificationNote: CONFIRMED against the printed 2019 edition: designAreaSqFt (19.3.3.1.4 sets the minimum area of sprinkler operation at 1500 ft2 for light/ordinary and 2500 ft2 for extra hazard), hoseStreamGpm and the duration ranges (Table 19.3.3.1.2 - light 100 gpm / 30 min, ordinary 250 gpm / 60-90 min, extra 500 gpm / 90-120 min), and maxCoverageSqFtPerSprinkler (Table 10.2.4.2.1(a)/(b)/(c)). NOT YET CONFIRMED: densityGpmPerSqFt, which has to be read off the plotted curves in Figure 19.3.3.1.1 and cannot be checked from the page's text. That is what keeps every row at 'verify'. Note the hose/duration table is 19.3.3.1.2 in the 2019 edition; reference/storage/fire-water-duration.json still cites the 2016 number 11.2.3.1.2 for the same data.
coverageNote: maxCoverageSqFtPerSprinkler is the MAXIMUM for the hazard, not the only value. Light hazard is 225 ft2 for unobstructed construction but drops to 200 ft2 obstructed and 168/130 ft2 for combustible construction with closely spaced members; extra hazard's 100 ft2 applies to hydraulically calculated systems with a density of at least 0.25 gpm/ft2 (90 ft2 under the pipe schedule method). A real design takes the figure for its own construction type from Table 10.2.4.2.1(a)-(d).
